planting.note: Pot divided offsets or purchased plants in a coarse, fast-draining bromeliad or orchid bark mix in spring through summer; Red Chestnut has no frost tolerance and should be grown outdoors only in zone 10-11 or brought indoors well ahead of cold weather elsewhere.

directions: This Brazilian-origin hybrid forms a broad, flattened rosette of glossy, strap-shaped leaves banded with creamy white that deepens to chestnut-red and rust-brown tones as the plant matures and receives brighter light. The slow-growing rosette eventually sends up a tall, branched flower spike with yellow blooms emerging from colorful bracts, though it is grown mainly for its long-lasting patterned foliage rather than its bloom. Keep the central cup filled with fresh water, provide bright filtered light or partial shade to develop the richest banding, and use a loose, bark-based mix rather than heavy garden soil. It tolerates lower indoor light better than many vrieseas, making it a popular choice as a houseplant as well as a shaded landscape accent in frost-free climates.

planting.note: Pot offsets or nursery plants in a light, bark-based bromeliad mix; Guzmania 'Hilda' has no frost tolerance and is grown as a houseplant or shaded container specimen outside of zone 10-11.

directions: Registered by Belgian breeder R. Deroose, this lingulata-type hybrid forms a tidy rosette of glossy, dark green leaves topped by a bold, star-shaped cluster of bright yellow bracts that holds its color for weeks at a time. Like other guzmanias it blooms only once per rosette before slowly declining, so the small plantlets that form around the base should be potted up separately to continue the display. Grow in bright, indirect light rather than direct sun, keep the central cup topped with water, and maintain the high humidity typical of its Central and South American rainforest origins. A well-draining bark or peat-and-perlite mix suits its epiphytic roots better than dense potting soil.

planting.note: Pot divisions or nursery plants in a coarse, fast-draining bromeliad mix; Maginali has no frost tolerance and should be grown in containers or shaded beds in zone 10-11, or as a houseplant elsewhere.

directions: Bred from discolor-type forms of Aechmea fulgens and Aechmea miniata, this fast-growing hybrid forms a wide, open rosette of soft leaves that are light green on the upper surface and contrasting maroon underneath, a two-tone effect visible whenever a breeze lifts the foliage. In season it sends up a large, dense panicle of small blue flowers that matures into long-lasting orange, berry-like fruits, adding color well after the bloom fades. Grow in bright, filtered light or partial shade to keep the leaf color from bleaching, and keep the central cup filled with water. Established clumps produce offsets freely at the base, which can be separated once they have formed their own roots.
